Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:12:1.hebrew: יליף בהמתך בהמתך משבת - מה להלן חיה ועוף בכלל, כדמפרש לקמי':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:12:1.english: Derive "your cattle" — "your cattle" from Shabbat - Just as there [regarding Shabbat], wild beasts and birds are included, as [the Gemara] explains further on.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:1.hebrew: בדברות הראשונות נאמר בהמתך - ולא נאמר בהן שור וחמור, ובדברות האחרונות הוסיף להזכיר שור וחמור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:1.english: In the first Commandments it is stated, "your cattle" - and "ox" and "donkey" are not stated in them, whereas in the second Commandments [Scripture] added to mention "ox" and "donkey".

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:2.english: And aren't [they] - They too were included in "all your cattle" that is stated alongside them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:3.english: Just as [with] ox and donkey that are stated here, undomesticated animals and birds [are] like them - And later on [the Gemara] explains the reason: [it is derived] from [the word] "and all" [in "and all your cattle"], which implies an inclusion.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:4.hebrew: אף כל - מקום שנאמר שור וחמור, כגון פריקה וחסימה ודומין להן, חיה ועוף כיוצא בהן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:13:4.english: So too, every - [place] where an ox and a donkey are stated — such as unloading and muzzling and [laws] similar to them — undomesticated animals and birds are like them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:17:1.hebrew: נכתוב רחמנא חד פרטא - ודרשינן כל דדמי ליה משני צדדין. מדכתב אידך, אם אינו ענין לדבר שנבלתו מטמאה, תנהו לענין עופות, דדמי לפרטא בחד צד, דהוו בעלי חיים דכוותיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:17:1.english: Let the Merciful One write one detail - and we would expound [to include] anything that is similar to it in two respects. Since [Scripture] wrote the other [detail], if it has no application to something whose carcass imparts impurity, apply it to the case of birds, which are similar to the detail in one respect, in that they are living creatures like it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:17:2.hebrew: כתב רחמנא שור - דלא אצטריך, דהא קדוש הוא בבכורה ומחמור קאתי. תנהו לענין סוסים וגמלים, דדמי לפרטא משני צדדין: נבלתו מטמאה ובעלי חיים הן, אבל עופות לא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:17:2.english: The Merciful One wrote "ox" - Which was not needed, for it is sanctified with firstborn [sanctity] and is derived from "donkey." Apply it to the case of horses and camels, which resemble the specific example in two respects: their carcass imparts ritual impurity and they are living creatures — but birds [do] not.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:18:1.hebrew: ריבויא הוא - ולא מדרש בכלל ופרט, וריבה הכל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:18:1.english: [It] is an amplification - And it is not expounded as a generalization and a specification, and [thus] it includes everything.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:1:1.english: But an ox, when it is of sound mind, [is] exempt - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:21:1.hebrew: פרי מפרי - ולד מולד, יין מענבים ושכר מתמרים, למעוטי כמהין ופטריות ומים ומלח דאינו פרי מפרי. וגדולי קרקע — למעוטי דגים, שאינן נקחין בכסף מעשר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:21:1.english: Produce of produce - Offspring [from] offspring, wine from grapes, and strong drink from dates — to exclude truffles and mushrooms, and water and salt, which are not produce of produce. And "grown from the ground" [serves] to exclude fish, which may not be purchased with [second-]tithe money.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:23:1.hebrew: השתא דאמרת כל ריבויא הוא - ואפי' עופות, למה לי דפרט בהמה ושור וחמור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:23:1.english: Now that you have said “all” [kol] is an amplification - [including] even birds, why do I need [Scripture] to specify “cattle” and “ox and donkey”?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:27:1.english: If so - that we derive [the laws of] diverse kinds from Shabbat.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:27:2.hebrew: אדם נמי ליתסר - למשוך בקרון עם הבהמה, דהא גבי שבת מוזהר כבהמה, דכתיב "ועבדך ואמתך ובהמתך":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:27:2.english: A person should also be prohibited - to pull a wagon with an animal, for regarding Shabbat [a person] is admonished like an animal, as it is written: "and your manservant, and your maidservant, and your animal."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:28:1.english: Papunaei - The people of Papunya, [which is] the name of a place.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:28:2.hebrew: רב אחא בר יעקב - מפפונאי היה, דאמרינן בהשותפין (ב"ב דף טז.), דריש רב אחא בר יעקב מפפונאי דשטן ופנינה לשם שמים נתכוונו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:28:2.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov - He was from Paphunya, as we say in [the chapter] HaShutafin (Bava Batra 16a): "Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov of Paphunya expounded that Satan and Peninah intended [their actions] for the sake of Heaven."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:28:3.hebrew: להנחה הקשתיו - עבד ואמה לבהמה, אבל לא לענין איסור אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:28:3.english: I have equated it concerning resting - [I have equated] a manservant and a maidservant to an animal, but not with regard to another prohibition.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:4:1.hebrew: מין בן דעת - היינו אדם, ואפי' הוא שוטה, מין בן דעת הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:4:1.english: A species [that is] mentally competent - That is, a human being; and even if he is an imbecile, he is [of] a mentally competent species.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:5:1.hebrew: שור חרש שוטה וקטן - שור שהוא חרש או שוטה או קטן או סומא, או מהלך בדרך בלילה, ואפילו הוא פקח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:5:1.english: An ox [that is] deaf, an imbecile, and young - An ox that is deaf, or an imbecile, or young, or blind, or walking on the road at night, even if it is of [standard] intelligence.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:1.hebrew: ולהפרשת הר סיני - "אם בהמה אם איש" כתיב, ואנן מרבינן חיה ועוף בגמרא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:1.english: And with regard to keeping [its] distance from Mount Sinai - "Whether beast or man" is written, and we include wild beasts and birds in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:2.hebrew: ולתשלומי כפל - ואע"ג דכתיב משור ועד חמור, שאר בהמה וחיה מרבינן בגמ', וכן בכולהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:2.english: And with regard to the payment of double - Even though it is written, "from an ox to a donkey," we include other [domesticated] animals and wild beasts in the Gemara, and so too in all of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:3.english: For unloading - [As it is written:] "you shall surely help unload with him" (Exodus 23:5).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:4.hebrew: לכלאים - דהרבעה, אע"ג דכתיב "בהמתך לא תרביע כלאים", הוי נמי חיה ועוף בכלל, כדיליף בגמרא. וכן לענין כלאים דהנהגה, ד"לא תחרוש בשור וחמור":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:6:4.english: With regard to diverse kinds - [That is,] of crossbreeding: even though it is written, "You shall not crossbreed your livestock with diverse kinds," wild animals and birds are also included, as derived in the Gemara. And similarly regarding diverse kinds of driving [animals together], [the prohibition of] "You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:7:1.english: Of what is common - Of something that is usual to occur.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:8:1.hebrew: חיה בכלל בהמה - דכתיב "זאת הבהמה אשר תאכלו", וכתיב בתריה "איל וצבי" (דברים י״ד:ד׳):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:8:1.english: An undomesticated animal is included in [the term] "animal" - For it is written: "This is the animal [behema] that you may eat," and it is written immediately after it: "deer and gazelle" (Deuteronomy 14:4[-5]).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:9:1.hebrew: לתשלומי כפל על כל דבר פשע על שור כו' כל דבר פשיעה - ואפי' דבר שאין בו רוח חיים, בפרק מרובה (לקמן בבא קמא סב:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:9:1.english: With regard to the double payment — "for every matter of trespass, for an ox," etc. — every matter of negligence - [This includes] even something in which there is no breath of life, [as is derived] in the chapter [entitled] Merubah (below, Bava Kamma 62b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 54b:9:2.english: From Shabbat - As it is written, "your ox and your donkey and all your cattle" (Deuteronomy 5:14).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:14:1.hebrew: בהמתך דדברות הראשונות כלל - לא חשיב ליה כלל ופרט המרוחקים זה מזה, דאחרונות וראשונות חדא מילתא היא, דזכור ושמור בדבור אחד נאמרו [ר"ה כז. שבועות כ:]:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:14:1.english: "Your cattle" in the first [version of the Ten] Commandments is a generalization - [The Gemara] does not consider this [to be] a generalization and a detail that are distanced from one another, for the latter and the first [versions] are one matter, as "Remember" and "Observe" were spoken in a single utterance [Rosh Hashanah 27a; Shevuot 20b]:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:16:1.hebrew: ואימא מה הפרט מפורש דבר שנבלתו מטמא - תימה: [א"כ] פרט ל"ל? דבכלל "בהמתך" נמי כתיב! ועוד: כשאומר "מה הפרט מפורש בעלי חיים, אף כל בעלי חיים" ועופות בכלל, היכי ס"ד דאתרבו עופות? לימא דכללא גופיה ממעט להו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:16:1.english: And say: Just as the detail is defined as an item whose carcass renders impure - [This is] astonishing: [If so,] why is the detail needed? For [this] is also written within the generalization of "your cattle"! And furthermore: when [the Gemara] says, "Just as the detail is defined as living creatures, so too all living creatures," and birds are included — how could it enter your mind that birds are included? Let [the Gemara] say that the generalization itself excludes them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:21:1.hebrew: פרי מפרי וגדולי קרקע - הכא משמע דבקר וצאן אקרי גידולי קרקע. ותימה, דבפ"ק דקדושין (דף יז.) גבי הענקה אמר, דאי כתב רחמנא "גורן", ה"א גידולי קרקע אין, בעלי חיים לא; כתב רחמנא "צאן". וי"ל, דלענין דבר היוצא ממש מן הארץ לא חשיב בהמה גידולי קרקע, ואין להאריך כאן יותר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 54b:21:1.english: Produce of produce and grown from the ground - Here it is implied that cattle and sheep are called "grown from the ground." And this is puzzling, for in the first chapter of Kiddushin (17a), regarding the severance gift [given to a Hebrew servant], [the Gemara] says that if the Merciful One had written [only] "threshing floor," I would have said [that] things grown from the ground — yes, [they are included, whereas] living creatures — no; [therefore] the Merciful One wrote "flock." And one can answer that with respect to something that emerges directly from the earth, an animal is not considered "grown from the ground." And there is no need to elaborate further here.
